response.sql: WITH per_coin AS (SELECT feecoin, AVG(NULLIF(rebtotal, 0)) AS avg_reb, AVG(CASE WHEN rebrate <> 0 THEN (rebrate - feerate) / NULLIF(feerate, 0) END) AS avg_gap FROM fees GROUP BY feecoin), bench AS (SELECT AVG(avg_reb) AS b FROM per_coin), kept AS (SELECT p.avg_reb, p.avg_gap, b.b FROM per_coin p CROSS JOIN bench b WHERE p.avg_reb > b.b) SELECT AVG(avg_reb) AS avg_of_avg_total_rebate, AVG(avg_gap) AS avg_of_avg_relative_gap, AVG(avg_reb - b) AS avg_excess_over_benchmark FROM kept

assumptions.assumption: Records with a NULL feecoin form one group, which counts as one currency in the benchmark mean. Currencies whose average rebate is missing are left out of the benchmark and are never kept.
A NULL rebrate or NULL feerate gives a missing gap, which is skipped in the average. A NULL rebtotal is skipped in the rebate average.
If no currency is kept, the query still returns one row with NULL values.
